Preserve all accepted requirements, public output contracts, other objectives, operations, bindings, IDs, navigation, selections, fact-resolution branches, header, document_write destination, and finally cleanup. This existing explicit structural revision authorizes only replacing assemble_product_record with deterministic typed scopes, their necessary captures, the resulting downstream flatten, and adding the missing complete-acquisition flag checks. Do not use discovery, weaken contracts, add unrequested work, or edit unrelated tasks.

Review findings: (1) assemble_product_record is kind:transform with omitted mode, so it invokes an LLM even though its prose says deterministic. It must become existing typed foreach/value/output bindings; no extract/interpret for assembly. (2) The four acquisition consumers check success and snapshot non-null but omit captureTruncated==false and manifestTruncated==false. Preserve the existing checks first and add both flags with binary short-circuit and predicates.

The exact replacement below has ALREADY compiled offline against this session's original discovered contracts using compact-bindings-v14, including WorkflowCompiler, with zero model/MCP calls. Apply it using the existing TaskPlan syntax. Omitted optional envelope fields keep normal defaults. Preserve the old operations and all other tasks exactly. No new primitive is needed. Nested foreach(maxItems:1) yields nested arrays: flatten once at each shown scope; after visit_products, rows is array<array<Product>>, so project_product_rows.items must flatten once. Capture the original visit item's href before entering new item scopes. The name and description captures are required ancestor bindings. They preserve nulls and exact source text; no array field/index access or manufactured scalar. Keep producer error_message as erreur. The resulting product records remain nonnull and fields nullable. Do not replace these bindings with another transform merely because the nested loops look verbose.
